summary: No fatal mathematical defect was found. The stated shared-draw population assumptions imply positive reliability calibration, edge-probability recovery, and score identification up to translation. Retain the conditional draft with local exposition corrections to the P convergence attribution, sufficient graph conditions, and empirical diagnostics. Those corrections do not change the central theorem. The acknowledged reuse of known calibration supports explanatory value but does not establish publication-level novelty or readiness.

findings.claim: The summary of P's convergence result needs sampling and regularity qualifications.
findings.evidence: inputs/r.tex:49; inputs/P.tex:361-376,698-725. P invokes uniform sampling and local curvature in its appendix and changes an approximate Taylor expansion into an equality without remainder control. A connected path with only one sampled comparison at a leaf need not have a finite unregularized MLE, regardless of the number of comparisons elsewhere.
findings.consequence: Correct the source attribution locally. This is not a counterexample to r: inputs/r.tex:78,100-109 require edge-specific population distributions and use direct inversion without MLE or a finite-sample rate.

findings.claim: Publication-level novelty is not established, although the stated explanatory contribution is supported.
findings.evidence: inputs/r.tex:24,37,112-114,128-130; inputs/r-references.bib:21-59. Inspected primary texts: https://arxiv.org/html/1706.06660 (Sections 2-4), https://arxiv.org/html/1904.11608 (Sections 3 and 5.1), https://arxiv.org/html/2310.02016 (Sections II and IV-B), https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10045 (Sections 3-4). Known work contains the calibration algebra and heterogeneous ranking methods, under models distinguished in the review.
findings.consequence: Set publication_readiness to NOT_ESTABLISHED independently of mathematical validity. Retain the conditional draft; known ingredients do not refute its theorem.

findings.claim: The graph discussion should explicitly distinguish sufficiency from necessity.
findings.evidence: inputs/r.tex:78,80-110,143. A five-cycle identifies positive skills through a_1^2 = (q_12*q_34*q_51)/(q_23*q_45), despite having no triangle. A calibrated connected spanning subgraph of the agent graph suffices for score recovery. Ma et al. (2019), Section 5.1 and Theorem 8: https://arxiv.org/html/1904.11608.
findings.consequence: Clarify the closing sentence of r.tex:78. The selected stronger sufficient conditions and theorem remain valid.

findings.claim: Passing the proposed moment diagnostics cannot verify the complete latent or strategic model.
findings.evidence: inputs/r.tex:149,155. An admissible positive triangle fits three reliability parameters without redundant equality restrictions. P already reports comparator cycle and likelihood diagnostics at inputs/P.tex:521 and accuracy at inputs/P.tex:550-552; these do not test r's observer calibration model.
findings.consequence: Describe moment tests as necessary observable checks, requiring additional overlap or edge-stratified replication for overidentification. Distinguish them from P's existing experiments.

findings.claim: The theorem follows from its actual stated assumptions, including at tied scores and perfect positive observers.
findings.evidence: inputs/r.tex:66-109. Binary conditional means imply 0 < a_r <= 1. Conditional independence on a common draw gives q_rs = a_r*a_s; the triangle fixes positive magnitudes, paths propagate calibration, b_er/a_r identifies m_e, and connected edge differences identify c modulo translation.
findings.consequence: The central claim SURVIVES. No fatal counterexample or broken proof step was found under the stated premises. Finite-sample conditioning is a separate issue.

findings.claim: The missing strategic mechanism and contribution semantics are adequately excluded from the conditional theorem.
findings.evidence: inputs/r.tex:43-45,118-124,134-149,160-161; inputs/Q.tex:1653-1734,1782; inputs/P.tex:285-303,337-349,385-389. Q requires known separated subjective belief maps and flexible transfers. P uses an external comparator and assumes equality to Shapley values. r expressly identifies the truthful-bootstrap, collusion, sampling, misspecification, and churn limitations.
findings.consequence: Retain as a conditional population draft, not a demonstrated incentive-compatible deployment. Learning objective report frequencies does not automatically recover Q's subjective belief maps.

limitations: Focused audit of all of r, its bibliography and supplied Q/P metadata, and relevant Q/P passages; no exhaustive audit of every source theorem.
Q and P were assessed from supplied files without a separate public-version identity check.
The bounded literature check inspected relevant full-text passages in four accessible primary sources; it is not exhaustive novelty verification.
References merely mentioned inside inspected sources were not treated as verified; no historical verdicts, peer notes, or unavailable internal notes were used.
External algorithmic convergence proofs were not independently validated, and r does not require them for its population proof.
No candidate compilation, experiment replication, repository tests, finite-sample bound, pipeline changes, other agents, or input modifications were performed.
